etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From late Middle English proprietee, propretee, propriete (“ownership”), borrowed from Anglo-Norman propreté, Middle French proprieté, from Latin proprietās. By surface analysis, prop(e)r +‎ -iety. Doublet of property.
senses: (obsolete) The particular character or essence of someone or something; individuality. [15th–20th c.]
